title: The even-degree intersection conjecture for partition path polytopes
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with terminal set $T$, and let $Q(G,\mathcal{T})$ denote the polytope associated with a partition $\mathcal{T}$ of $T$. A vector is **$\mathcal{T}_1-\mathcal{T}_2$-feasible** when it is feasible for paths between the parts prescribed by partitions $\mathcal{T}_1$ and $\mathcal{T}_2$ of $T$. **Even-degree intersection conjecture.** If all degrees of $G$ are even, then for any two partitions $\mathcal{T}_1$ and $\mathcal{T}_2$ of $T$, every vertex of

$$
Q(G,\mathcal{T}_1)\cap Q(G,\mathcal{T}_2)
$$

is $\mathcal{T}_1-\mathcal{T}_2$-feasible; equivalently,

$$
Q(G,\mathcal{T}_1)\cap Q(G,\mathcal{T}_2)
$$

is the convex hull of the $\mathcal{T}_1-\mathcal{T}_2$-feasible vectors. The conjecture would make it possible to optimize arbitrary objective functions over $\mathcal{T}_1-\mathcal{T}_2$-feasible vectors, extending the known result for maximizing the sum of coordinates; the general case is presented as unresolved in the source.
source_name: Mouna Sadli and András Sebő, “Jump-systems of T-paths”, arXiv:2302.13448 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.13448

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).
